reviews.text: Im super disappointed in this title honestly. the vibe, the world, all seem really unique and interesting but its just WoW with 1995 graphics sadly from everything from mechanics to professions, with the same gameplay loop and everything. I didnt play for long enough to give a "fair" review but after playing for like an hour I realized I could just go play classic wow where there will at least be other people to play with. I hope to see some originality out of this title, something to look forward to besides just being a worse version of other mmos.
5 Minutes In: This looks terrible. I'm closing the app after killing a deer and a boar. 2 Hours In: OK this is fun. I'm hooked. Just have to pick a few more Dew Leaf before I log out.
It's fun. A lot of ideas taken from WoW, but that's not a bad thing. Movement is a little clunky and that may be a turn-off for some people but outside of that it has a lot to do and is fun.

Trolddom is an open world exploration MMORPG with elements like Auction House, professions, and questing centered around party play and adventure Its oldschool artstyle is incredibly coherent and very charming, its audio and SFX fit the world very well There are many dungeons for an initial 1.0 release, especially with its max level being 30. Itemization is alright, and stat values could use a stat squish. The class design is sort of lacklustre, but the gameplay itself is still addicting and lots of fun. Will see improvements and glad game has lots of potential The game also features an offline-specific mode in case that's your kind of thing

Finally a fully released indie MMORPG. The only one of the year and it's actually good, feels like 2D WoW - go quest with your buddies and explore. You're not sitting in one spot grinding the same mobs for 10 hours. It's been fun. https://youtu.be/JFMzetG84pw

Quite literally a 2D version of Vanilla WoW. I'm playing a fighter which has all the best abilities of the WoW Warrior + new and engaging abilities. Combat is super fun. Items are fantastic and getting item upgrades, crafting materials and basically anything feels great. You start getting your first decent pieces of gear around level 5 and even start getting helmets and shoulders around level 10. If you aren't bothered by the simple 2d graphics, you'll find this is a fantastic spin on the proven WoW MMO formula we all grew to love, but this time with redefined rules, a completely mysterious world and lots of new little systems that keep it feeling fresh. I'm honored to have found this before its popularity exploded! woot!

Trolddom is a standout gem with great class diversity, tons of quests, and impressively polished content. Every class talent tree feels unique, and the world is fun to explore. The community is incredibly welcoming, making the whole experience even better. Highly recommended!
If you're looking for a tight-knit community and engaging content, look no further. This game is awesome for what it is and for the price. Highly recommend!

probably best 2025 mmo. its new and feels a little rough, some things i dont like are not being able to inspect people/no character customization. When you equip gear there is rarely any visual difference, which is a huge part of mmorpgs imo, being able to show off your stuff and show your individuality. also why is there no friends list? no multiple action bars? basic things that should exist just arent here. but otherwise its great. its pixelated wow basically. if you like wow youll like this, no question.
unironically the best mmo I have played in recent years, even tho the graphical style isnt my cup of tea and the movement is a bit clunky.
The only other 2d mmo that has sucked me in this much was UO.

Wow! 10/10. After putting some time into the game, which involved me playing almost 5 hours past my bedtime, and thinking about it when I woke up, I felt I needed to say, how highly I recommend this game. Two locked characters that are fun to unlock, and aren't another pay wall, and no pay to win!

I wasn't expecting much, but the lvling/talents/proffessions/classes and world has pulled me in for several hours.. Finally unlocking the Paladin, I'm very much keen to keep playing tomorrow. Played the Demo for 3 hours and I had to buy it. Also great to see the developer actively patching/doing updates.

I only lost a few hours, but the game is basically World of Warcraft in 2D — there are skills, a skill tree, interrupts, dungeons, items divided into categories. Sure, the movement can be a bit annoying and the hero could use some animations, but those are just details. The game is absolutely worth the money spent.

Game is fun so far and the developer seems very open to feedback. Check it out if you suffer from WoW nostalgia. For a brief moment you will immerse yourself and forget that you are in your 30's clinging onto your teenage gaming years.
WOW Classic/ OSRS Combined Good Game
It's 2D Wow but without gnomes. 10/10

Game has a lot of potential, feels like a top-down WoW classic. However, I can't recommend this game due to it's use of OpenAI for "non-important NPC dialogue". I don't think it's that hard to write dialogue yourself, even as a solo developer. I'll change my negative review if that ever changes.

A wholly unconvincing attempt at capturing 'old-school' nostalgia. Despite boasting an enticing open world with a plethora of regions to explore, they are, unsurprisingly, bland and uninviting. 350+ quests, yet not a single quest falls outside of the cookie cutter, fetch/return or kill X amount of Y. With 0 memorable characters, questlines or engaging character dialogue, everyone and every area becomes forgettable and a slog to play through. Similarly, traversing the world seems entirely without thought, due to the lack of teleportation and restriction of mounts until you're 2/3 of the way through available content. With this being the case, if you dare to explore your own way, by the time you get to certain regions, you will be completely over-levelled, leading to every single quest in a region being pointless as XP rewards scale with level. Dungeons/Elite mobs are, in all respects, inaccessible to solo players unless you are drastically over-levelled, at which point the quest tied to them will grant no real effective reward so are pointless. While one may argue that Dungeons are made to be completed in a group, they provide no interesting gameplay to engage the players outside of mobs having more health and damage. The community is nice despite being made up of max level players simply waiting for more content, and I can appreciate how much work the solo dev has put into this game. Nevertheless, the game is awful and is an insult to time investment for what it has to offer.
Easily the best MMORPG of the 2025!

This game was a wonderful gem of an experience, made by a single dev, but not really playable due to low playercounts. It took a fair bit of coordination in the Discord server to get through the first one in the game. Still, great work whomever!
Game is great, scratches something deep inside my dormant brain. Deserves WAY for attention than it's getting. Solo dev who included an offline mode and custom server api on release. Love this game.

I’ve not cleared the first dungeon yet, but I’m enjoying this game a ton. I’ve played approximately 2 hours of vanilla WoW so the comparisons are lost on me. I’m a RuneScape oldhead. Trolddom aggressively rewards exploration. The amount of little nooks and crannies to explore make the world feel so much more alive than you would expect from something of its scale. As an example: I popped into a little forest pathway I spotted in a copse of trees. It led to a clearing with an altar to an underworld god. Why is it there? How long has it been there? Is someone sneaking away from town to worship an underworld god in a secluded glade? Who knows. Your guess is as good as mine. There is no quest (that I’ve found yet). There is no reason to be there, unless you want to up your devotion to that god. Nobody told me it was there. I stumbled upon it. This will happen a lot if you just walk around. You’ll find random quest-starting items. You’ll find random altars. Random people. You will find yourself surprised that a kinda grungy 2D pixel world feels more alive and mysterious than most things you’ve played in the last decade. Feels kinda Arthurian. Monmouth, not the prancy French stuff. This game benefits immensely from being new, small, and obscure. No one has figured out optimal quest order. There is no meta build for condemnation priest. No one has figured out how to manipulate game ticks to speed up herbalism training (if you don’t play RuneScape don’t look this up, it will make you sad). Hopefully, this game will continue to grow until those things inevitably happen. It’s a natural consequence of playerbase growth. But in the mean time, you have no choice but to experience the game. The experience is not “new.” It’s not novel. It’s an action bar + tab targeting MMO. If you’re reading this, you’ve already played at least a half dozen of those. Nothing I’ve experience yet is truly groundbreaking. But it FEELS FRESH. Just try it. Try the demo. Or buy the game because it’s $10 and this single developer has done something really cool. Buy it because it’s $10 now and maybe it’ll be the “””WoW Killer””” in a few years. Do whatever mental gymnastics you need to. But try this game.

If I had to sum up this game in two words it would have to be: "Deceptively Fun". Do not let the low-poly fool you where this game lacks in the graphic department it makes up for with its multitude of systems. From old school divinity worship with associated buffs to collecting RNG recipes, equipment, mats and if that doesn't wet your appetite all archetypes have three subcategory talent trees that you can put points into at your own leisure and an NPC that allows you to reset at any point if you don't like what you've done setting you up with ease of access to test build theory along with a world of dungeons/bosses to test them on. You cannot level all professions on one character which gives you an incentive to level alts other than just checking out builds, or mules for space. Leveling is just the right amount of grind "for an old school experience" if you are one of those people that thinks you need to be maxed in two days this isn't the game for you.

Great game apparently made by just a single dev, you can tell it's a passion project. Pretty decent community but sadly for now I have to give it a negative I wish there was a neutral option. I do recommend the game in it's current form but sadly I'm leaving a negative till something is done with the auction house. Pages and pages of single listings of items people will probably never want anyway. It's literally impossible to just look through the auction house without clicking a bunch of category filters. I know the dev more than likely won't see this as they don't seem to come to Steam at all but I don't have discord installed and haven't used it in years and not going to start. Anyway when this game starts feeling like a job just because of the auction house searching then something is wrong. The game badly needs a way to filter out certain traders by name or something. Once there's something in the game that makes the auction house a better experience then I'll change the review to a positive, maybe this will get the devs attention not everyone wants to be on discord all the time. Your game is one Steam maybe come here once a week and look at the platform that your game is actually on. I have suggestions for the game in the discussions I think would make it better and once again not going on discord.

I really enjoyed the beginning of the game. I got about as far as the goblin quests before I had to stop and refund. The character movement occurs tile-by-tile and was a little jarring to me. I never get motion sick from video games, not even VR, but I'm just not able to handle movement in this game. Something to consider if you suffer from motion sickness. Plays like WoW classic, like some other reviews mentioned. Go kill these things, pick up this item, and I will give you this choice of gear. Casting spells and abilities, looting, and even item drops are very reminiscent of WoW. The talent trees are small but seem to offer more substantial options compared to incremental 0.2/0.4/0.6/0.8/1 options you would see in WoW. If movement was ever smoothed out, I would come back in a heartbeat. I guess I expected something more similar to how movement appears in RPG MO. This game was scratching an old-school MMO itch that I haven't been able to reach for quite some time now.

I got to lv 17-20 ish over the course of 33 hours Need more players but the game is FUN and a bit of a GRIND also need PARTY for dungeons. There is tanks, dmg dealers - bow/caster/melee/2hand/all kinds armor sets and bonuses and crafting galore plus fishing but I couldnt keep playing without people my lvl guild was way above me and always busy

Scratches the itch for a casual classic-style mmo. Quests are your typical go grind & fetch, but the gear upgrades and talent trees feel impactful and it's fun to see the future upgrades you'll get. If you like chill indie or classic style mmo's (WoW) and can stand the graphics, you'll likely find a fun and familiar game here.

Awesome old school rpg. I'm really enjoying the community, quests, and combat/non-combat skills. I am leveling up fishing and cooking while playing as a warrior like class. I'll probably buy a few copies for friends if they get into the demo as much as I did.
Sad to see i was the only player online, the dev has absolutely abandoned this project.

I don't leave a lot of steam reviews but I am really enjoying this game. A mix of old school d2 exploration with a bit of WoW mixed in, would be great to see more players in the world to run dungeons. Worth the 10 bucks for sure.

"She ain't the prettiest, but she's got a heart of gold and puts-out whenever you want." When's the last time you heard that and it was true? Well, with Trolddom, it's true! Not only does she have heart, she's charming, witty, playful and, at times, even trying. As you flirt with her, imploring her to give-up her secrets, she feigns dissidence before reneging with playfully compliance; with but a hint of challenge, and an air of yet more to come. What's not to enjoy about that? Sure, she's a bit simple at times, but she won't let you down. She'll wrap you softly, warmly, in her arms; enveloping you with beautiful simplicity of heart. (Spent 40.9 hours in demo version, on 3 characters; purchased game at 19.2 hours into demo experience - no regrets)
